To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we determined the structure of the YscUP interaction interface and that we show that the YscU autoprocessing event may serve as a timing switch for T3SS substrate secretion.
we have identified the YscP interaction interface on YscU and characterized the YscUC and YscI interaction interfaces.
the substrate specificity switch protein YscP binds to the C-terminal domain in YscU with high affinity, and that this interaction protects YscU from self-cleavage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the molecular details of a protein-protein interaction network in a type III secretion system.
the molecular details of protein-protein interactions that play a central role for the function of T3SSs.
the identification of the YscUP interaction interface and the characterization of the role of this protein-protein interaction in the regulation of T3SS substrate secretion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the YscP interaction interface on YscU is a novel target for the development of anti-T3SS drugs.
YscP binds to the C-terminus of YscU and that the binding of YScP to YscU protects YscU from autoproteolysis.
YscU is a central hub in the regulation of the T3SS, which is involved in the regulation of substrate specificity, substrate delivery, and the timing of the secretion process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction of YscU, the substrate specificity switch, with the inner rod component YscI is regulated by the interaction between YscU and its cognate regulator YscP.
the YscU/YscP/YscI complex represents a novel type of protein complex that is important for the regulation of the T3SS.
the YscP interaction site on the C-terminus of YscU plays a central role in regulating the T3SS substrate specificity switch.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the YscP-YscU-YscI interaction interface may be an attractive target for the development of anti-infective compounds.
the Yersinia T3SS has a sophisticated molecular mechanism to ensure the timely secretion of the appropriate set of effector proteins.
the YscP protein acts as a substrate specificity switch by binding to YscU and thereby inhibiting YscU autoprocessing, which in turn leads to the secretion of early substrates.
